parts.label: Part 3
parts.article:
Part three. You will hear two students and their tutor discussing their business reports and theoretical analysis tools. First, you have some time to look at questions twenty-one to twenty-five.

Now listen carefully and answer questions twenty-one to twenty-five.

Hi, Francis, Sam. So how did you go with applying the different theoretical business tools for the report I asked you to write?

It was interesting and made us really focus on which tool was best to use when analyzing a business.

Good. So tell me what you found out.

We liked the theory behind PEST analysis. That's political, economic, social, and technological. Although we're not sure if it was very applicable to our case. Some of the other groups had studies for which it worked really well, and they said it was easy to use. But I felt it focused too much on the big picture and was unsuitable for our company.

I agree. On the other hand, I enjoyed using the drill down method. It was painstaking to do, and we seemed to be working on it for ages, but the results were worth waiting for.

Yes. I liked the way it eventually broke down complex problems.

Yes. I much preferred doing the PMI analysis. It was so straightforward to break down into its three components: plus, minus, and interesting implications. You just needed to brainstorm these components and then write them up. Fast and effective, and it didn't make your brain hurt doing it.

I agree. And you don't need any special training at all. Anyone can use it.

Hmm. So was there any tool that you thought was superior to the others?

In my opinion, the one tool that is critical to business, especially for larger companies, is Pareto analysis. If they apply Pareto analysis, they would see that by focusing on the critical twenty percent of their problems, they could generate eighty percent of the benefits. This would allow them to work faster, and it also reduces their workload. It's all about finding out what their basic problems are.

I agree with Francis about Pareto, but my favorite was the SWOT analysis. You know, looking at the company's strengths, weaknesses, opportunities, and threats, as it can be used in so many different situations. It works in large and small companies and even down to departmental level. It was great for our case study.

Yes, that's true.

Before you hear the rest of the discussion, you have some time to look at questions twenty-six to thirty on page six.

Now listen and answer questions twenty-six to thirty.

Okay. I've read your draft report, but can you tell me a bit more about that company you focused on?

Well, the company we used in our study was a manufacturing company who have relied on distributors to take their product to the end user. We did some analysis examining the possibility of them distributing their own products.

We initially looked at their strengths. The company, although it is small, is well-known and has a very good reputation. The management are very committed to increasing the company profits, and they are confident this move would be successful.

Right. And the company has quite a lot of staff who have previously worked for distribution companies, so the knowledge is already there. That was something we didn't expect to find and is probably going to help them the most to achieve their goals.

I was quite impressed by some of the opportunities you detailed. I did think you missed something quite pertinent to their future growth, however.

What was that?

You didn't consider the potential for establishing an offshore division. You talked about the company negotiating better terms with its suppliers. Most of these are based abroad, and so if the company had a way of actually distributing the product there, this could be a tremendous opportunity and give them an edge over their competitors.

That's a good point.

So what did you think about the threats we identified?

I thought you did a good job. I was really pleased to see that you considered how the government's planned environmental policy could really affect the viability of this venture.

With this law being introduced next year, they might need to find new ways of using their existing technology. It's easy to identify what your competitors are doing, but it's the bigger picture that often gets ignored.

So, Sam, what did you learn from this assignment?

Heaps. I guess I hadn't realized how much time it takes to ensure your company survives and profits. It was great to study the different tools in books, but applying them in the real world was much harder than I thought. It was a great learning experience.

I'm glad I could make your assignment relevant.

I'm basically happy with your report. You've got the format correct with the necessary headings, et cetera, and you've got sufficient details under the different headings. Just remember to state whether or not you think the company should go ahead with the new venture. But you've done a good job so far.

That is the end of section three. You now have half a minute to check your answers.

analyses.content: 录音中直白地说觉得PEST分析关注点太大，“不适合（unsuitable）”他们的公司，直接对应选项C。
Some of the other groups had studies for which it worked really well, and they said it was easy to use. But I felt it focused too much on the big picture and was unsuitable for our company.
你可能会听到“easy to use”就去选E，但请注意，那是录音里提到的“其他组（other groups）”的看法，并非说话人自己的评价。
On the other hand, I enjoyed using the drill down method. It was painstaking to do, and we seemed to be working on it for ages, but the results were worth waiting for.
你可能会因为后面跟了句“worth waiting for（结果值得等待）”而犹豫，或者听到“painstaking”想选F（难应用），但这里通篇在强调这个过程特别费时间。
录音里说做这个分析很费力（painstaking），感觉做了“好久好久（for ages）”，这对应的就是选项D的“耗时太长”。

It was so straightforward to break down into its three components, plus, minus, and interesting implications. You just needed to brainstorm these components and then write them up. Fast and effective, and it didn't make your brain hurt doing it. I agree. And you don't need any special training at all. Anyone can use it.
你可能会听到“break down”这个词就和上一个工具Drill Down混淆，千万别走神，这里只是在讲PMI的具体操作步骤。
录音中两人连番夸奖这个方法直接（straightforward）、快（fast），而且不需要特殊培训“任何人都能用（Anyone can use it）”，妥妥对应选项E“易于使用”。

If they apply Pareto analysis, they would see that by focusing on the critical twenty percent of their problems, they could generate eighty percent of the benefits. This would allow them to work faster, and it also reduces their workload.
录音开头提到了“larger companies（大公司）”，你可能会没听完整就去选了G（适合所有规模），但录音只是说这对大公司很关键，并没有说所有规模都适用。
录音中指出这个方法能让人工作得更快，还能“减少工作量（reduces their workload）”，完美对应选项A的“节省时间和精力”。

I agree with Frances about Pareto, but my favorite was the SWOT analysis. You know, looking at the company's strengths, weaknesses, opportunities, and threats, as it can be used in so many different situations. It works in large and small companies and even down to departmental level.
只要不被上一题的“Pareto适合大公司”绕进去，听到“large and small”就能稳稳拿下这道题，干扰非常小。
录音直接提到这个方法在“大公司、小公司甚至具体部门（large and small companies and even down to departmental level）”都起作用，契合选项G的“适合几乎所有规模”。

groups.description:
What comment is made about the seasonal changes in pollen in each of the following European countries?
Choose FIVE correct answers, A-G, next to question 21 – 25.

questions.question: What does Frances consider as the best strength of the company?

analyses.content: 女声（Frances）在男生说完后补充说，公司有很多在分销公司工作过的员工（staff），并强调这才是“最能帮助他们实现目标的（help them the most）”，对应选项B“有经验的员工”。

Right. And the company has quite a lot of staff who have previously worked for distribution companies, so the knowledge is already there. That was something we didn't expect to find and is probably going to help them the most to achieve their goals.
你可能会因为最先听到名声好（reputation）和管理层（management）就匆忙选了A或C，但那是男生Sam说的，读题一定要注意题目问的是Frances（女声）认为最好的优势是什么。

questions.question: What factor did Sam overlook for the future growth of the company?

analyses.content: You didn't consider the potential for establishing an offshore division. You talked about the company negotiating better terms with its suppliers. Most of these are based abroad, and so if the company had a way of actually distributing the product there, this could be a tremendous opportunity and give them an edge over their competitors.
你可能会听到供应商（suppliers）或者竞争者（competitors）想选A或C，但录音里提这些词是为了说明建海外分部带来的好处，真正被他“忽视（didn't consider）”的核心动作是建海外分部。
教授明确指出Sam没有考虑到建立“海外部门（offshore division）”的潜力，offshore division直接同义替换选项B的overseas office。

questions.question: Which of the following can be the threat to a company?

analyses.content: I was really pleased to see that you considered how the government's planned environmental policy could really affect the viability of this venture. With this law being introduced next year, they might need to find new ways of using their existing technology.
你可能会听到现有的技术（existing technology）或竞争者（competitors），但这只是在新法律背景下需要面对的具体挑战，真正的“威胁源头”是新颁布的法律。
教授指出政府计划出台的环保政策会影响公司生存，并在下一句明确说这项“法律（law）”明年就要推行了，law对应选项C的“新法规（legislation）”。

questions.question: What has Sam learned from the research?

analyses.content: I guess I hadn't realized how much time it takes to ensure your company survives and profits. It was great to study the different tools in books, but applying them in the real world was much harder than I thought.
你可能会听到“time”、“survives and profits”就去联想选项B（成功企业的成本），但这里整个句子的核心逻辑在“but”之后的反转，现实应用难才是他最大的感悟。
Sam感叹在书本里学理论是一回事，但在“真实世界里应用（real world）”却难得多，体现了书本理论和现实之间的落差，对应选项C。

questions.question: What is the professor’s suggestion for the report?

analyses.content: You've got the format correct with the necessary headings, et cetera, and you've got sufficient details under the different headings. Just remember to state whether or not you think the company should go ahead with the new venture.
你可能会听到“format correct”或“sufficient details”就觉得是B（重组结构）或C（加细节），但教授说的是他们在这两点上已经做得非常好了（You've got...），完全不需要再改。
教授在最后建议，报告里务必要明确陈述公司“是否应该继续（whether or not you think the company should go ahead）”这项新业务，这就等于选项A的“给出一个最终的决定”。
